**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: three hours.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will be penalised.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorised composition will be severely sanctioned.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d)** Life is better in the city than in the countryside. Do you agree?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: state a position (partial agreement).
2. For the city: education, health, jobs, services.
3. Against the city: cost, crowding, pollution, crime, loneliness.
4. For the countryside: clean air, cheap food, community, calm; weaknesses are a matter of policy.
5. Conclusion: it depends on the person and on development of both.

**Model composition (508 words)**

Every year thousands of young Cameroonians leave their villages for Douala, Yaounde or Bamenda, convinced that the city holds the key to a better life. Their parents, meanwhile, often insist that the village is the only place where a person can live in peace. The claim that life is better in the city than in the countryside therefore deserves careful examination. In my view, the city offers undeniable advantages, but it is far from superior in every respect.

The strongest argument in favour of the city is opportunity. Cities contain most of the country's universities, hospitals, banks and companies, so a young person can find education, specialised treatment and a wide choice of jobs. A farmer's son who wants to become an engineer, a nurse or an entrepreneur can usually do so only in an urban setting. Cities also provide services that remain scarce in many villages: regular electricity, piped water, good roads, internet connection, libraries and markets that stock everything. In an emergency, an ambulance or a police patrol is far more likely to arrive quickly in town than in a remote hamlet.

However, these benefits come at a heavy price. City life is expensive: rent, transport, food and school fees consume salaries that look generous on paper. Many migrants end up jobless in overcrowded neighbourhoods, squeezed into tiny rented rooms. Traffic jams, noise, floods caused by blocked gutters and air polluted by exhaust fumes make everyday life exhausting. Crime, too, is more common where strangers outnumber neighbours. Worse still, the city can be lonely, for people live behind high walls and often do not know who lives next door.

The countryside, by contrast, has treasures that money cannot buy. The air is clean, the food is fresh and cheap, and the land provides a livelihood to those prepared to cultivate it. Communities are close, and a funeral, a wedding or a poor harvest is shared by everyone. Children grow up with space to play, respect for elders and knowledge of their culture. Stress, which causes so many illnesses in towns, is much less severe, and neighbours still greet one another by name. It is true that villages often lack hospitals and schools, but this is a weakness of policy, not of the place itself. When governments build roads, clinics and electricity networks in rural areas, village life improves dramatically, and the gap with the city narrows.

Ultimately, a good life depends less on the place than on the person and on the way the place is organised. A hard-working person can prosper in a village through modern farming, and an unemployed young man can be miserable in the finest city, surrounded by luxuries he cannot afford. For this reason, I agree with the statement only in part. The city is better for those who seek education, specialised careers and modern services, but the countryside is better for those who value peace, health and community. The wisest course is for the nation to develop both, so that no citizen is forced to choose between opportunity and happiness.

**Marking grid (20 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Saying "I agree" or "I disagree" and listing points for one side only, with no counter-argument.
2. Writing a list of ideas with no linking words, so that the essay does not read as a continuous argument.
